what: Whether the test suite would catch a bug, measured by writing bugs into the decoder
why: a green suite says nothing about what it would have caught. Everything else in this report measures the decoder; this measures the thing that measures the decoder
method: `tools/mutants.py`: change one load-bearing constant, run `cargo test --workspace`, record whether anything failed and which test, undo it with `git checkout --`. Each mutation is a bug someone could write -- a table entry off by one, an index base, a scale factor, a channel mapped to the wrong input -- not a random character. The run refuses to start on a dirty tree

per_mutation.mutation: the block-offset step, 32 -> 31
the steep switch, one slot back -> none
the steep switch, one slot back -> two
dequantisation, nquant 96 -> 95
dequantisation, the 820 scale -> 821
the smooth ramp, ts + 1 -> ts
the WAVE mask of the left channel
the interchange rank of an unmapped location, 32 -> 0
the JOC input of the left surround, 3 -> 4
the height pair of configuration 4 mapped like configuration 1
the OAMD sample-offset table, 8 -> 9
the ramp-duration table, 32 -> 33
the matrix alignment, 10 -> 9
the sparse chain, measured -> as printed
the TrueHD major-sync CRC polynomial, 0x002D -> 0x002F
the restart-header CRC polynomial, 0x1D -> 0x1F
the substream CRC initial value, 0xA2 -> 0xA3
the DAMF y coordinate, front and back swapped
a dropped dependent substream no longer makes a stream unclean
the programme verdict ignores a dropped dependent substream
the programme verdict counts a second programme as unclean

the_two_holes_it_found.the_oamd_sample_offset_table: changing the first value from 8 to 9 left every test passing
the_two_holes_it_found.the_ramp_duration_table: changing the first value from 32 to 33 left every test passing
the_two_holes_it_found.why_those_two: both are transcribed numbers from tables 23 and 25 with no structure to check them against, which is exactly the kind of constant a typo survives in, and both reach the timing of every metadata update
the_two_holes_it_found.fixed_by: `the_timing_tables_are_the_ones_the_clauses_print`, which writes both tables out again rather than reading the constants it pins. The mutations are caught now
the_two_holes_it_found.and_it_found_something_on_its_first_run: the last entry of table 25 is 2048 while clause 5.6.2.9 puts `ramp_duration_bits` in [0, 2047], so the index reaches one duration the explicit field cannot express. The first version of that assertion had it backwards and failed

the_survivor_that_should_survive.why_no_unit_test_can_catch_it: there is no specification behind it. It was fitted against Dolby's decoder, so only a comparison with another decoder can judge it
the_survivor_that_should_survive.what_does_catch_it: the media suite. With the alignment changed by one slot, `the_steep_switch_is_measured_where_the_branch_is_the_common_case` fails: the reading in use gives 52,44 dB against Dolby and the printed one 52,07, and the gate asks for a decibel of margin

reading: all fourteen are caught, thirteen by unit tests and one by a media test. That is a measurement of the suite rather than a claim about it, and the two holes it found were real
